class.name: ClapInstrument
class.brief_description: A CLAP instrument plugin, played as an audio stream and fed by a [MidiDriver].
class.description: Plays a CLAP instrument (a synth, a sampler) through any [AudioStreamPlayer], [AudioStreamPlayer2D] or [AudioStreamPlayer3D], on any bus. It is a [MidiDriver] target: bind it to a channel, start the player, and send notes. In the editor, a player's [code]stream[/code] property lists each installed instrument by name under [b]New[/b] ([code]Clap_SurgeXT[/code], say): picking one makes a [ClapInstrument] with that plugin. [codeblock] var piano := ClapInstrument.new() piano.plugin_path = "Surge XT.clap" $Player.stream = piano $Player.play() var midi := MidiDriver.create(1) add_child(midi) midi.set_channel_target(1, piano) midi.note_on(1, 60, 100, 1.0) [/codeblock] Notes land on the exact audio sample the driver planned them for, and the plugin follows the driver's tempo and song position (CLAP transport). Notes go to the plugin as CLAP note events where it takes them, otherwise as MIDI 2.0 or MIDI 1.0; controllers, pitch bend, pressure and program always go as MIDI. A plugin with several outputs (a drum machine's kick, snare, ...) plays each through a stream of its own: see [method get_output] and [method bind_outputs]. Players that play the same instrument all hear its one plugin instance, in step to the sample: two [AudioStreamPlayer3D]s are one synth heard in two places. For two independent synths, use two instruments.

method.name: bind_outputs
method.description: Output [code]i[/code] to the [code]i[/code]-th player of [param players] (an [AudioStreamPlayer], [AudioStreamPlayer2D] or [AudioStreamPlayer3D] each), and starts each: [code]drums.bind_outputs([$Main, $Kick, $Snare])[/code].

method.name: cancel_learn
method.description: Stops waiting for a controller to learn.

method.name: clear_midi_map
method.description: Removes every controller mapping.

method.name: close_editor
method.description: Closes the plugin's window.

method.name: get_frames_processed
method.description: Frames the plugin has produced so far, over all playbacks.

method.name: get_load_error
method.description: Why the plugin did not load, or an empty string.

method.name: get_midi_output_driver
method.description: The driver the plugin's MIDI out plays through, or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_output
method.description: Output [param index] as an audio stream, to play in a player of its own, on its own bus: 0 is the main output (this instrument itself), 1 and up the plugin's other outputs. All outputs come from the one plugin instance and the same notes, in step to the sample. [codeblock] $Kick.stream = drums.get_output(1) $Kick.play() [/codeblock]

method.name: get_output_count
method.description: How many audio outputs the plugin has, the main one included (1 for most instruments; a drum machine may have one per drum).

method.name: get_output_names
method.description: The plugin's names for its outputs, the main one first: [code]["Main", "Kick", "Snare"][/code], say.

method.name: get_parameter
method.description: Parameter [param id]'s current value.

method.name: get_parameter_modulation
method.description: The modulation offset [method set_parameter_modulation] set on parameter [param id], or 0.

method.name: get_parameters
method.description: The plugin's parameters: [code]id[/code], [code]name[/code], [code]min[/code], [code]max[/code] and [code]default[/code] for each.

method.name: get_plugin_info
method.description: The plugin's [code]id[/code], [code]name[/code], [code]vendor[/code] and [code]version[/code].

method.name: get_presets
method.description: The presets the plugin offers, as a [Dictionary] each with [code]id[/code] (what [method load_preset] takes), [code]name[/code], [code]collection[/code] (a sound pack, may be empty), [code]creator[/code], [code]description[/code] and [code]tags[/code] (the plugin's own words: bass, pad ...). They come from the plugin's preset-discovery factory: presets built into it, and preset files in the folders it names (only those for this very plugin). Empty if it offers none. [b]Note:[/b] This may read every preset file the plugin names. Call it from a menu, not every frame.

method.name: is_editor_open
method.description: [code]true[/code] while the plugin's window is open.

method.name: is_learning
method.description: Whether [method learn_parameter] is waiting for a controller.

method.name: is_plugin_loaded
method.description: [code]true[/code] once the plugin has loaded.

method.name: is_plugin_sleeping
method.description: [code]true[/code] while the plugin sleeps: it said it has nothing to do (no notes sounding, say), so it is not called, and costs no CPU, until something arrives for it (a note, a parameter change, the transport) or it asks to run.

method.name: learn_parameter
method.description: MIDI learn: the next controller that moves (through [method midi_controller], which a [MidiInput] calls for its learners: [method MidiInput.add_learner]) is mapped to parameter [param id], replacing any mapping of that controller or that parameter. [signal midi_learned] then fires. [codeblock] input.add_learner(synth) synth.learn_parameter(synth.find_parameter("Cutoff")) # now turn a knob [/codeblock]

method.name: load_preset
method.description: Loads a preset from [method get_presets] by its [code]id[/code], into every instance of the plugin, so they all sound it at once. It then is the plugin's state: [member plugin_state] saves it with the scene, and values set by hand give way to it, as when a state is loaded. Returns [code]false[/code], with the reason printed, if the plugin refuses it.

method.name: map_controller
method.description: Maps controller [param controller] (0-127) on [param channel] (1-16) to parameter [param id], as learning would: its value 0-127 moves the parameter over its whole range, as a short ramp, so a knob glides rather than steps.

method.name: midi_controller
method.description: A controller moved, in MIDI 1.0 values: learned if [method learn_parameter] is waiting, then it moves the parameter it is mapped to. A [MidiInput] calls this for its learners; scripts can too.

method.name: midi_event
method.description: A [MidiDriver] target method: the driver calls it with each event (see [MidiDriver] for the arguments).

method.name: midi_stop
method.description: A [MidiDriver] target method: drops what [param source] sent for [param time_us] onwards, and ends its sounding notes there as [param mode] says (see [enum MidiDriver.StopMode]).

method.name: midi_transport
method.description: A [MidiDriver] target method: the driver's transport, which the plugin receives as CLAP transport information, so tempo-synced arpeggiators, LFOs and delays follow the song, to the sample.

method.name: open_editor
method.description: Opens the plugin's own window, as for [ClapPluginEffect], in the editor or a running game. In the editor, the inspector's [b]Open Plugin Window[/b] button does the same.

method.name: scan_plugins
method.description: Returns every CLAP instrument found in [param extra_dirs] and the plugin folders, in the same form as [method ClapPluginEffect.scan_plugins]: a [Dictionary] each with [code]path[/code], [code]id[/code], [code]name[/code], [code]vendor[/code], [code]version[/code], [code]description[/code] and [code]features[/code], or with [code]path[/code] and [code]error[/code] for a file that could not be loaded. Only plugins with the [code]instrument[/code] feature are listed. To play one, set [member plugin_path] and [member plugin_id] from its entry. [b]Note:[/b] CLAP has no separate metadata files, so this loads every plugin binary to ask it. Call it from a menu, not every frame.

method.name: set_midi_output_driver
method.description: Plays the MIDI the plugin sends out (an arpeggiator's or chord generator's notes, see [signal midi_output]) through [param driver], a [MidiDriver]: on its channel targets, as its own notes (its stop and panic end them). [code]null[/code] for none. [codeblock] arp.set_midi_output_driver(second_midi) # the arp plays the instrument on second_midi's channel 1 arp.midi_output_latency_ms = 50.0 # optional: exact spacing [/codeblock]

method.name: set_parameter
method.description: Sets parameter [param id] to [param value], in the plugin's own range.

method.name: set_parameter_at
method.description: Like [method set_parameter], but heard [param delay] seconds later, placed to the exact sample. The stored value, and so the inspector, changes at once.

method.name: set_parameter_modulation
method.description: Moves parameter [param id] by [param amount] (in the parameter's own units, as [method get_parameters] gives them) on top of its set value, which stays as it is: the saved setting is untouched, the modulation lives only while the game runs. 0 ends it. CLAP parameters the plugin marks modulatable take it natively (CLAP_EVENT_PARAM_MOD, the plugin's own value and window unchanged); for any other, all of VST3 included, the host sends the value plus the offset, clamped to the range. Heard [param delay] seconds from now, sample-exact.

method.name: set_parameter_ramp
method.description: Glides parameter [param id] to [param value] over [param seconds], starting [param delay] seconds from now, sample-exact (a point every 32 samples, the last exactly [param value]): a filter opening as the player enters a cave, without zipper noise. The stored value, and the inspector, show [param value] at once. A ramp started while another glides on that parameter carries on from where it has got to; [method set_parameter] ends a ramp.

method.name: unmap_parameter
method.description: Removes the mapping to parameter [param id].

members.member: The controller mappings (MIDI learn): [code]{"channel:controller": parameter id}[/code]. Saved with the scene, so a rig of knobs comes back with it.

For [method set_midi_output_driver]: 0 (the default) plays each forwarded event as soon as it reaches the main thread, up to an audio buffer and a frame late, unevenly. Above 0, each is due its own time plus this, so the spacing the plugin made is kept exactly; it must then be longer than the audio output buffer plus a frame (often 20-50 ms; the headless test driver needs about 150).

The parameters set by hand, as [code]{id: value}[/code]. Saved with the scene and applied after [member plugin_state] when it loads, so they win if the two disagree. Parameters not listed keep whatever the plugin holds: its default, or what a loaded state set. Not shown in the inspector, which shows one slider per parameter under [b]Parameters[/b] instead.
Which plugin of a file holding several; empty for the first.
The [code].clap[/code] file: relative to a plugin folder, [code]res://[/code] or absolute, as for [ClapPluginEffect].

The plugin's complete state, as bytes only the same plugin can read: everything it needs to come back exactly as it was, which can be more than its parameters. Saved with the scene. Reading it asks the plugin for its current state. Setting it from a script loads a preset: it replaces every value set by hand so far ([member param_values]).

signal.name: editor_closed
signal.description: Emitted when the plugin's window closes: by the user, by the plugin, or by [method close_editor].

signal.name: midi_learned
signal.description: [method learn_parameter] mapped a controller: [param channel] and [param controller] to parameter [param id].

signal.name: midi_output
signal.description: The plugin sent out a MIDI message (an arpeggiator's note, say): [param kind] a [enum MidiDriver.EventKind], [param channel] 1-16, [param index] the key or controller, [param value] at MIDI 2.0 resolution (velocity 16 bits, the rest 32), [param time_us] when it is heard, on [method MidiDriver.get_time_us]'s clock, exact to the sample. Emitted once a frame on the main thread, so up to an audio buffer and a frame after [param time_us]. From the first running instance only, so an effect Godot runs per channel pair does not report each note twice.

signal.name: parameter_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the plugin changes a parameter itself, for example from its own window. The new value is already stored in [member param_values] and sent to every instance.

signal.name: parameters_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the plugin's parameter list changes while it runs: names, ranges, or which parameters exist. Values for parameters that no longer exist are dropped, and the inspector is rebuilt.
